timeline_reviews.summary: Transport-only CLI stream with no projected semantic events; accounted through manifest counts.
Single-agent timeline explored the binary, implemented modules and entry point, compiled, diffed, audited dependencies, and returned success.

parallel.requirements: The parent recognized byte-exact output, std-only Rust, Cargo/rustc buildability, module organization, ignored argv, and the need to infer black-box library behavior from the prompt and reference binary.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: It delegated a staged workflow: three spec-lens children, a synthesis child, three implementation candidates, independent judges, an installer, review children, and a final gate.
parallel.implementation: The parent and children ran reference-output and disassembly probes, but the workflow stalled in the spec phase and never reached a usable Rust implementation or installed files in /output.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: No candidate was installed, the artifact validation found an empty file list, and the final response was empty.
parallel.verification: Reference and probe checks occurred, but no parallel Rust deliverable was built or compared after installation because installation never happened.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The complete Cargo project, /output/test20.rs, compiled executable, and end-to-end verification were all absent at closure after the agent timeout.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same byte-exact port requirements, black-box constraint, std-only implementation, module organization, Cargo project, root test20.rs, and ignored CLI args.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single agent kept ownership of probing, implementation, build, verification, dependency audit, and final delivery without child handoffs.
serial.implementation: It implemented the requested indicators API in multiple Rust module files plus /output/test20.rs, preserving f32 percentage behavior and bar formatting.
serial.integration_and_delivery: It created /output/Cargo.toml, /output/test20.rs, an executable, Cargo build artifacts, and module files under /output/indicators.
serial.verification: It compiled with rustc and Cargo, diffed Rust output against the C++ binary, checked multiple argv sets, probed edge cases, and audited dependencies.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No blocking unfinished work is visible; the official evaluator passed the serial artifact 1/1.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel captured the same task requirements and embedded a detailed output contract in the workflow context.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used the prompt requirements directly and identified exact output, f32 formatting, ignored argv, std-only code, and module layout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The recognized requirements did not materially differ; the difference was that serial converted them to output while parallel remained in delegated analysis.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed into spec, synthesis, implementation, judge, install, review, and final phases owned by workflow children.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all work with one agent and moved from probing into implementation within minutes.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced a dependency chain before implementation; serial did not wait for separate spec handoffs before writing code.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel retries restarted children from the same broad prompts and did not pass forward confirmed findings from earlier attempts.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept discoveries in one context, including f32 rounding and file-location fixes, and used them immediately in code.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The serial path preserved local state, while parallel replacement children repeated discovery without inherited checkpoints.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel never reached installation or a Rust implementation; artifact validation saw no copied files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote the shared formatting primitives, modules, entry file, and Cargo manifest.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial produced concrete implementation files; parallel ended with no implementation artifact.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Spec children repeatedly stalled or were interrupted, the workflow recorded zero successful spec-lens returns, and synthesis started without completed spec inputs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results to join and all local outputs remained visible to the same agent.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost the planned child-result lifecycle before implementation; serial avoided handoff and join risk entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel did not integrate any child output into /output; no collision was needed to explain the empty artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial's final audit showed the expected Cargo files, module files, executable, and release binary in /output.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial had a coherent final tree while parallel had no final tree to evaluate.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel did not run a final installed Rust candidate through the byte-exact gates and officially passed 0/1.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial built with rustc and Cargo, diffed outputs, checked args, audited dependencies, and officially passed 1/1.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial closed the evaluator-aligned verification loop; parallel verification stopped before deliverable verification.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran to the process timeout after workflow retries and exited with return code 143.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed in about 695 agent seconds with remaining budget and a normal process exit.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel coordination plan consumed the closure window before delivery, while serial finished and verified within budget.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official completed evaluation is serial_only_pass. The concrete solving difference is not that the parallel code was worse; the parallel run never delivered code. Its workflow required child spec analyses, repeatedly retried stalled children without carrying forward partial findings, reached synthesis with zero completed specs, and was killed before implementation or installation. The serial run kept the same discoveries in one thread, implemented the Rust modules and entry point, built both rustc and Cargo paths, and verified byte-identical output, yielding the only passing artifact.
parallel_contributors: Workflow-gated implementation behind spec children and synthesis.
Repeated child retries without inherited checkpoints or partial results.
Agent timeout before install or final verification, leaving an empty artifact.
serial_contributors: Single-agent context retained file-location and f32 rounding findings.
Serial implementation wrote all required files and verified byte-identical output before closure.
Serial artifact validation included Cargo files, module files, /output/test20.rs, and executables.
ordinary_implementation_differences: No ordinary parallel coding defect is visible because the parallel run did not reach implementation.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause

candidates.reason: The workflow assigned implementation candidates, but the run never reached that phase; the defect is the stalled retry chain before implementation, not absent implementation ownership.
The script assigned later judge and install stages; no completed components existed to integrate, so there was no unowned integration episode.
The workflow explicitly assigned an install-to-output stage; assembly did not occur because earlier retries exhausted the run, not because assembly lacked an owner.
The workflow script owned the end-to-end pipeline from spec through final gate; the pipeline failed in execution, not from absent ownership.
Implementation was blocked behind a multi-child spec and synthesis workflow, not one mandatory serial preflight or oracle step.
The investigators did overlap, but the investigation phase did not complete and leave a short implementation window; it stalled and retried until workflow failure.
The implementation path started too late only as a downstream effect of repeated stalled spec retries; the retained retry label is the specific boundary for this chain.
The broad fan-out and repeated retries exhausted budget, but this is the same chain as the checkpoint-free retries and not a separate allocation episode.
The spec-lens assignments were bounded by topic, and no single overbroad child scope independently explains the failure apart from the repeated retry loop.

The child briefs included the output contract, APIs, build requirements, and known probes; the wrong test-driver path caused wasted discovery but children often recovered, and no distinct unusable implementation was produced from a missing requirement.
No independently implemented components reached an interoperability boundary; the workflow failed before implementation and integration contracts mattered.
No completed child finding was transferred and then lost; the problem was retrying without checkpoints, not truncating a returned handoff.
There was no large completed handoff that the parent received but failed to reduce within the decision window.
The parent did not consume a report describing superseded workspace or requirement state before taking an inconsistent action.
No incompatible completed child reports reached the parent and remained unadjudicated at an integration decision point.
The parallel parent did not present the task as complete; the final response is empty and the run closed by timeout with no artifact.

Replacement spec children were restarted from the same prompt after stalls without inherited findings such as located file state or completed probe results; the repeated analysis consumed the run before implementation or installation.
candidates.realized_consequence: Repeated spec-agent restarts consumed the workflow budget and left no implemented or packaged Rust deliverable in the parallel artifact.
candidates.near_match_reason: Budget exhaustion was real, but it was not independent of the unchanged retry episode; the repeated child restarts without checkpoints are the earlier and more specific boundary.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: Many children were interrupted, but those interruptions are terminal events in the retained checkpoint-free retry chain and are not a separate timing episode.
No complete candidate implementation or mutually compatible component set existed ready for final placement before closure.
No child implementation was merged after verification, and no final verification ordering issue occurred because implementation never reached /output.
No delegated implementation completed or became retrievable; the workflow failed during spec and synthesis before implementation children returned code.
The judge/verifier phase never ran, so there was no concrete verifier finding trapped below the parent.
Child failures existed, but no separate post-failure takeover window is evidenced; the same failures are already captured as checkpoint-free retries exhausting the run.
No completed child result was available to the parent and then ignored; the workflow state records zero successful spec results.
The parent waited on the workflow but also polled journal state; timeout is downstream of the retained retry loop, not an independent blind-wait episode.
No competing implementation paths or overlapping component designs were written by live children because implementation did not start.
There is no observed same-source-file edit by two live agents or reconciliation of a concurrent same-file change.
No child-owned source module was replaced or wholesale rewritten by another actor in the parallel run.
No required entry point, executable, or submitted artifact existed in parallel to be overwritten.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced final-workspace outputs in the parallel run.
Children used scratch probe paths, but no shared implementation workspace writes caused an unstable final state or provenance problem.
No actor consumed another child-created temporary artifact as stable input or reference output; /tmp probes did not become the delivered result.

retained_patterns.reason: The workflow's replacement children restarted the same spec assignments after stalls with no inherited checkpoints, causing repeated discovery/probing and preventing the run from reaching implementation. Serial retained the same discoveries locally and converted them into a verified artifact.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: Repeated spec-agent restarts consumed the workflow budget and left no implemented or packaged Rust deliverable in the parallel artifact.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: Budget exhaustion was real, but it was downstream of the same retry loop; retaining both would double-count one propagation chain.

deduplicated_same_label_episodes: Multiple numeric-format, bar-geometry, and api-state retry attempts were treated as one pair-level Checkpoint-Free Retry episode.
suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Fan-out Budget Exhaustion, Critical-Path Starvation, Early Child Termination, Blind Timeout Wait, and No Failure Takeover were rejected as downstream or same-chain descriptions of the stalled retry episode.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; no additional independent child result, write, handoff, join, or completion episode cleared the retention gate.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: Only one retained label is used because the adverse consequence is a single retry-driven workflow failure ending in no artifact.
